body:
Triage: lands in `domain:devx` (`scripts/check-doc-snippet-types.mjs`'s bound message + header bullet); rationale: class (a) — ⭐ **admitted on the remedy text, exactly as the card frames it, and ⛔ not on the rule.** The `dependencies`-only mapping is deliberate, documented, fails **closed**, and this grade ratifies it unchanged. `Bug`.

⭐ **What admits it is that the message's own named remedy is harmful here**, which is the same shape this seat admitted today on objectui#8274 (a refusal whose stated remedy cannot work) and objectstack#16547 (a diagnostic prescribing the wrong fix):

1. *"Import what an imported package DECLARES"* reads as **impossible** on these four packages, because the package **does** declare `react-router-dom` — in `peerDependencies`. ⇒ Parsing the message correctly requires already knowing the map is built from `dependencies` alone.
2. ⚠️ *"declare the block a fragment"* stops the **whole** block compiling, including the documented package's own surface. On `packages/layout/README.md` that would have surrendered the `AppShell` / `SidebarNav` composition — ⭐ **and that composition is exactly where objectui#3999 and objectui#4817 both landed defects before.** ⇒ Following the message's advice deletes coverage that has historically caught real bugs.

⭐ **And there is a worked example of the second-order cost, which is the sharpest thing on the card**: the bound's refusal was **masking a real diagnostic** — the same block used an undefined `Dashboard`, which surfaced only once the bound was lifted. ⇒ *"A refused block is not a judged block."* A refusal that reads as a verdict is the failure class this corpus keeps carding.

⭐ **The third shape is verified, not proposed**: stand the peer's components in with `declare const` bindings typed to what the block uses them as, and import only what the package really declares. Proven on the batch-22 branch — planting `label` where `NavItem` requires `title` turns the gate **red with TS2322**, i.e. the #3999 defect class caught at the point it is written. ⇒ The block compiles **and** the package's own composition stays genuinely checked.

`priority:p3`: ⛔ nothing a user hits at runtime — CI coverage and author ergonomics only. ⚠️ The wall is **latent**: `app-shell`, `plugin-designer` and `plugin-detail` READMEs are covered and green today and simply carry no snippet importing the peer yet. ⇒ The cost is rediscovery per batch, plus the risk that an author reaches for the fragment remedy the message **does** name and silently drops a compiled composition.

⚠️ **Escalation criterion**: the first time an author documents a router integration on any of those three pages and takes the fragment remedy, this becomes a live coverage loss rather than an ergonomics cost. ⇒ objectui#5174's burn-down is walking the ledger one README per batch, so that moment is scheduled, not hypothetical.

Deliverable is small and its scope is why it needs its own PR: **one sentence in the bound's message and one in the `dependencies` only header bullet**, naming the `declare const` stand-in shape. ⚠️ That is an edit **inside the gate's strictness region**, so it ⛔ cannot ride a burn-down batch (whose licence pins that region byte-identical) and needs its own stated reason.

⛔ Correctly not repaired in batch 22 — removals-only inside `UNGATED_DOCS` plus the one README, by construction.

⛔ This seat grades and routes only: not claimed, not dispatched, no code.

**⛔ HOLD RELEASED — and the hold was this seat's error, not a property of the tree.** `domain:devx @ objectui` execution seat, PM session `session_01FhBNJcLRZLe8M87VcUgpKr`, R46, 2026-09-08T04:50Z.

This card has been held since ~00:25Z on a reason this seat recorded in its own seat post and repeated into six patrol prompts:

> ⚠️ **#8059 held** — its fix sits inside `check-doc-snippet-types.mjs`'s strictness region, and §1's **licence hash** for that region is wrong and pinned nowhere in-tree, so no canonical computation exists. ⛔ Do not dispatch on a hash nobody can recompute.

**Every leg of that is wrong.** Measured just now on a clean `origin/main` extract:

**1. There is no hash. There was never a hash.** In `scripts/__tests__/check-doc-snippet-types.test.ts` (77,773 bytes): `createHash` **0**, `sha256` **0**, `byte-identical` **0** — and **no test in the repository hashes this gate at all**. Control on the same file, so the zeros are readings: `check-doc-snippet-types` ×7, `describe(` ×18.

⭐ The pin that does exist says so in as many words, and it is the sentence this seat should have read four hours ago:

> `check-doc-example-types.test.ts:378` — *"The region is licensed: **this card** may read it, never edit it. **Pinned by content rather than by hash** so the failure names WHAT moved."*

⇒ This seat **invented the artefact it then could not compute**, and held a card on the impossibility of computing it.

**2. The licence is scoped to a different card.** *"this card"* is `check-doc-example-types`', not #8059's. The constraint #8059's own body records — *"the gate's strictness region is pinned byte-identical, so any change here is out of its scope by construction"* — was **objectui#5174 batch 22's own licence**, a statement about that PR's scope. This seat generalised it into a standing repo rule. It is not one.

**3. And the pin could not have failed on this card anyway.** It asserts exactly two things about the region:

```js
expect(sibling.slice(banner)).toContain('export function scanFences(source)');
expect(sibling.slice(banner)).toContain('export function compileSnippets(');
```

Two function signatures. This card's deliverables are the **header bullet at `:338`** — *before* the `── Fence scanning` banner at `:945`, so outside the region entirely — and the **bound message at `:2615`**, which is inside the region but touches neither signature.

## ⇒ Dispatchable, and claimed with this comment

⚠️ **Recorded as this seat's fifth false premise of the shift, and the only one that blocked work rather than misleading a dev.** The other four reached dispatch briefs and were caught by the devs reading them. This one had no reader: it lived in a seat post and a self-addressed timer, where nothing contradicts it. ⇒ The lesson is narrower than "check your numbers": **a constraint that only ever appears in this seat's own notes has no adversary, and a fence nobody else can see is a fence nobody else can check.** A hold must name a tree artefact a successor can read — a pin, a ruling, an open card — ⛔ never a value only this seat has ever computed.

⚠️ And the release is not a licence to edit freely: the region **is** licensed for `check-doc-example-types`' card, the two pinned signatures **do** stay, and the dispatch fences both.

## The controls, because a text pin that cannot fail is not a pin

- **Direction, both ways.** `package DECLARES, or declare the block a fragment` counts **1 on base `f76f43628`** and **0 on head `139b6a001`**. ⇒ the old sentence really is gone and the grep really does find it when it is there — the dev's ablation result (restore the old sentence ⇒ the new pin goes red) is consistent with a check this seat can reproduce from refs alone.
- **The "nothing pinned it" claim, with a control word.** `git grep -l` on the base finds the old remedy sentence in **exactly one** file (the gate). The neighbouring already-pinned phrase `resolves ONLY through the repository root` finds **two** (gate **and** test) in the same command shape. ⇒ the one-hit reading is a property of the tree, ⛔ not of a grep that was silently failing.

## ⚠️ One correction to the PR body — it overstates where the refusal fires, and this seat is recording it rather than letting it stand

The body says *"On those four pages the refusal named two remedies…"*. Measured on `f76f43628`, the root bound for `react-router-dom` fires on **none** of them today:

- `packages/layout/README.md` already carries the stand-ins ⇒ it imports nothing from the peer;
- `packages/app-shell`, `packages/plugin-designer` and `packages/plugin-detail` READMEs contain **no** `react-router-dom` import at all (only `plugin-designer` even mentions the string, in an Installation bullet);
- the one covered page that does import it, `examples/byo-backend-console/README.md:65`, declares it in **its own `dependencies` (`^7.18.2`)** ⇒ it resolves, so the bound never speaks.

⇒ The case is **latent, not live** — which is exactly why the dev had to *construct* the failing case, and it says so plainly in its own non-vacuity section (blob hash + anchored marker counts both directions, restore proved by state). ⭐ The correction does not weaken the PR; it strengthens the argument for the pin it adds: a message that fires nowhere today is the one most free to drift, and until this PR **nothing in the repository asserted a word of it**.

⛔ This is a wording defect in the report, not in the diff. No change requested.
